definitions.explanation: Used to indicate that something is nothing more than what is stated; emphasizes limitation or simplicity.

examples.japanese: {単|たん}に{運|うん}が{良|よ}かっただけだ。
examples.english: It was simply that I was lucky.

examples.japanese: これは{単|たん}に{参考|さんこう}のためです。
{単|たん}に{知|し}らなかったのではない。{無視|むし}したのだ。
examples.english: It wasn't that he simply didn't know. He ignored it.

notes:
USAGE PATTERNS:
- {単|たん}に〜だけ: simply just ~
- {単|たん}に〜のではない: not simply/merely ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {単|たん}に: Simply, merely (emphasis on limitation)
- ただ: Just, merely (more casual)
- ただ{単|たん}に: Simply, merely (emphatic combination)

NUANCE: {単|たん}に often implies 'nothing more than' or 'only this,' sometimes with a dismissive or minimizing nuance.
